steps.title: Three platform groups
notes: Gas flow, build order and scanning order are platform parameters (FLAGS.PLATFORM): they belong to the whole build plate, not to one part. ATU reads them from the profile that is set as the platform profile.

The scanning order group is generated from the vector type table: one number per vector type, smaller numbers first. The defaults expose supports first, then the hatches, then the contours from the inside out.

lines: // sort_models: order the parts along the gas flow (downstream first);
// not used by the mode 'global' (there the parts are no sort level).
// Name = vector type name, one shared description for all entries.

steps.title: Read the platform settings
notes: read_platform_settings reads the build order by the index of the chosen option, not by its translated text, so the result does not depend on the user interface language.

steps.title: Downstream first
notes: flow_direction turns the angle into a unit vector: 0° flows to +X, 90° to +Y. downstream_key is the negative position along that vector, so an ascending sort puts the islands furthest downstream first. The spatter then lands on islands that are already exposed.
Islands within the same 1 mm band count as equally far downstream; then the island id decides.

steps.title: The sorter settings
notes: build_sorter_config collects mode, gas direction and scanning order once per call. With Sort models against gas flow, the parts on the plate are ranked along the gas flow as well; the island grid is a single part, so the model rank does not matter here.

steps.title: One key tuple per mode
notes: Every path gets a tuple of numbers; the first entry decides, then the next. Platform starts with the scanning order: all hatches (40) of the plate, then all first borders (80). Island starts with model, supports and the gas flow bucket, and puts the scanning order behind the island id: one island after the other, and inside an island the scanning order decides.
That is why, in the video, First border 80 → 5 makes every island start with its border: 5 is now smaller than the 40 of the volume hatch.

lines: return [a_item.model_rank, a_item.support_rank, a_item.island_bucket, a_item.islid, a_item.order, a_item.orig];
// No model, support or island entry: all paths of one vector type
// are sorted by their own position only.
// sort_models = true: inside one vector type, the gas flow
// position is more important than the model order.

steps.title: Global: every path by its own position
notes: The mode Global has no model, support or island entry in its key: after the scanning order come the position of the path itself along the gas flow (1 mm bands) and its position across the flow. make_item computes both from path_center, the centre of the path's own bounds.

A hatch block is one stripe, chess field or hexagon cell, so the blocks of a long part and of the small parts next to it are exposed in one sweep against the gas flow, as in the second video. On the island grid every island has a single hatch block, so Global differs from Platform only where islands are equally far downstream: there the position across the flow decides instead of the island id.

steps.title: Write the exposure order
notes: sort_layer builds the items of all paths of the layer (all parts together, because the laser exposes the plate in one sequence), sorts them and writes the position as _processing_order. No path is moved: the host and the exporters read this number. The colour mode Exposure order in the videos is a colormap of exactly this attribute.
The sorting is the first step of the post-processing: the laser assignment, the power optimization and the time estimate all work along this order afterwards.

recipes.title: Island by island by default
recipes.why: Each island is finished before the laser moves on, so its border is melted while the hatch is still warm.
recipes.result: New profiles start with the build order Island. The platform profile decides, so create the new profile and set it as platform profile.

recipes.title: Global by default
recipes.why: Plates with long parts and striped or chessboard hatches: one sweep against the gas flow over all parts.
recipes.result: New profiles start with the build order Global: every hatch block and contour is placed by its own position. Sort models against gas flow has no effect in this mode.

recipes.title: Borders before the hatch
recipes.why: A defined edge first, then the inside, as in the second change of the video.
recipes.result: The first border gets the scanning order 35, below the 40 of the volume hatch. In the Island mode each island starts with its border; in the Platform mode all borders come first.

recipes.title: Another default gas direction
recipes.why: A machine whose gas flows from front to back (towards +Y).
recipes.result: New profiles assume a gas flow towards +Y: the islands are exposed from the back row to the front, and the limitation window of the hatch rotation turns with it.
